This file's feature is the quiz SCORING itself, so it is a separate manifest per discover-before-create.
*** WHY THIS IS UI-DRIVEN AND NOT pure apiTests (the load-bearing honesty boundary) ***: the
ONLY deterministic quiz scoring in the whole product is CLIENT-SIDE. CopilotAssessmentLanding.tsx computes score+band
in-component from quizData.ts VALUES; NO network call fires on completion (the only quiz POST is a
separate lead-capture, out of scope for scoring), so there is NO scoring endpoint to hit with an
apiTests call. The server-side quiz path that DOES return a score+recommendedService
(POST /api/quiz/submit, artifacts/api-server/src/routes/quiz.ts) is NOT deterministic and cannot be
asserted input->output here: it (1) scores the 5 categories with a LIVE Claude call
(model claude-haiku-4-5, quiz.ts:472-494) — non-deterministic and billable per run — and (2) derives
recommendedService from the DB-seeded Lead Offer Engine (lead-offer-engine.ts) over
leadOfferInferenceRulesTable / leadOfferRuleGroupsTable + a second AI pricing call. Those rule tables
cannot be seeded from this harness (no DATABASE_URL in Claude Code sessions), and the AI is not a
stable contract, so 'this exact answer combination -> this exact score+service' is architecturally
unassertable against that endpoint. Asserting only that /api/quiz/submit returns SOME tier in the
enum would be the 'did it return something' smoke check this task explicitly rejects, so it is
deliberately NOT faked here. The deterministic client-side scoring, asserted below with exact
hand-computed values, is the real regression coverage. (The deterministic total->tier boundary math
at quiz.ts:496-501 — sum of five 0-10 category scores; cutoffs 16/26/36/46 — is genuinely testable,
but only downstream of the non-deterministic AI total, so it is not reachable as pure input->output.)
SCORING MODEL (verified against src/pages/home/quizData.ts + CopilotAssessmentLanding.tsx:304-307, NOT assumed):
VALUES = [0.18, 0.45, 0.7, 0.95] indexed by the chosen option (A/B/C/D).
wedges = the 6 PILLAR answers (CopilotAssessmentLanding.tsx answers[1..6]) mapped through VALUES (unanswered -> 0.1).
score  = Math.round( (sum(wedges) / 6) * 100 ).
band   = score>=80 'Advanced' | >=60 'Established' | >=40 'Developing' | else 'Early'.
QUESTIONS[0] is the CONTEXT/seat-count question (pillar -1); answers[0] sets the cohort phrase
ONLY and does NOT affect score. There are 7 questions total, so 7 clicks complete the quiz and
flip `done` true (the result card renders only when done). Each click answers the CURRENT question
and advances (CopilotAssessmentLanding.tsx pick()), so a combo is expressed as the ordered click sequence Q0,Q1..Q6.
EXACT COMBOS ASSERTED (each score is Math.round(sum(6 pillar VALUES)/6*100); Q0's answer is the
first click and never enters the sum):
A) UNIFORM baselines (each also proves no pillar is stuck at the 0.1 default — a dropped-pillar
regression shifts the exact value):
all-A  -> pillars 0.18x6 -> score 18  -> 'Early'.
all-B  -> pillars 0.45x6 -> score 45  -> 'Developing'   (adds the previously-uncovered
'Developing' band AND the previously-unexercised option B).
all-C  -> pillars 0.70x6 -> score 70  -> 'Established'.
all-D  -> pillars 0.95x6 -> score 95  -> 'Advanced'.
B) MIXED-per-pillar (the strongest catch for a VALUES-index or pillar-ordering regression — every
pillar carries a different option, so a wrong index map / off-by-one / mis-summed pillar moves
the exact score off the asserted value):
(57 and 78 are safely clear of the .5 rounding knife-edge and of every band boundary.)
C) CONTEXT-EXCLUSION probe: Q0=D then pillars all-A -> score MUST still be 18 / 'Early' (identical
to all-A). A regression that started counting answers[0] (e.g. an off-by-one that indexed
answers[0..5] instead of answers[1..6]) would put the D at Q0 into the sum and change the score,
so this combo fails loudly on exactly that class of bug while all-uniform combos would not.
HOW THE SPECIFIC SCORE IS ASSERTED (the load-bearing part): the framework's uiStep `expect` action
asserts element STATE ONLY (visible/hidden/present/absent — see UiTestExecutor.EvaluateExpectAsync);
it has no enforced DOM-text assertion (see the textContains caveat below). The score is dynamic text
inside quiz-result with no per-score testid, so CopilotAssessmentLanding.tsx exposes scoped data-score={score} /
data-band={band} attributes on the quiz-result div (CopilotAssessmentLanding.tsx:521). An ATTRIBUTE SELECTOR
([data-testid='quiz-result'][data-score='57'][data-band='Developing']) then asserts the exact
score+band via genuine element presence — a wrong/unchanged result makes that selector NOT match and
the step fails.
textContains CAVEAT (honest): Git #1016 added a uiSteps[].textContains field, but on the current
code it is ONLY plumbed loader -> AutomationAction; UiTestExecutor.EvaluateExpectAsync does NOT yet
read it, so a textContains assertion is currently SILENTLY NOT ENFORCED. It is therefore intentionally
NOT used as coverage here — the data-score/data-band attribute selector is the real assertion.
Each combo re-navigates with `goto /LP/copilot-assessment` to reset React state (fresh mount: step 0, answers all null) —
there is no data-testid on the in-page 'Start over' button, and a fresh navigation is the cleanest
reset.
